title: friction-check candidate handoff - tomas rivera
content:
Candidate: Tomas Rivera
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference-serving) — oncall + kernel-fiddle + model rollouts
Interviewer: Carmen Ortega (owning doc)
Round: Final loop (pair + system design + oncall simulation)
Quick summary:
- Strong systems intuition, clear ownership language.
- Code pairing was pragmatic: used a small working prototype, focused on incremental correctness rather than clever one-liners.
- Design portion shows latency-first tradeoffs; had useful ideas around KV cache sharding and memory-aware batch sizing.
- Main risk: limited throughput-facing benchmarking experience on heterogeneous GPU fleets (less on collecting microbenchmarks and building regression harnesses).

Scorecard (1-5):
- System design & architecture: 4
- Production judgment & tradeoffs: 4
- Debugging / oncall simulation: 3
- Coding (correctness, clarity): 4
- Performance optimization instincts: 3
- Team fit / communication: 5
- Overall recommendation (fast check): Strong hire, contingent on pairing with senior perf/infra mentor for first 6 months.

Notes to self (informal):
- In pairing, Tomas defaulted to simpler data structures (good) but deferred deep kernel/allocator details when pressed — said he'd "reach for flamegraphs and microbenchmarks" but couldn't produce a recent example where he owned that end-to-end.
- Very explicit about past ownership: one project where he rebuilt a batching pipeline to reduce tail latency. Good ownership narrative — drove spec -> infra -> rollout. Ask ref about the rollout phase (can they speak to incidents or regressions?).
- On telemetry: wants more structured SLOs per model signature; suggested using per-route histograms + sampling of prompts when latency passes threshold. Not novel but practical.
- On latency/cost tradeoffs: advocated adaptive batching + lax quota fallback; also suggested fallbacks to smaller quantized variants — knows the right knobs but less clear on implementation complexity surface area across kernels.

Oncall simulation (3):
- Struggled with the initial noisy-alert triage (took a few minutes to articulate hypothesis tree). Once hypothesis formed, bisected to a bad rollout config. Good escalation instincts and calm.
- Would benefit from tighter crisp hypotheses next time; maybe probe to see whether they have run significant incident postmortems as author.

Take-home and test notes:
- Take-home (mini perf test) looked fine functionally but lacked a thorough benchmarking section (no reproducible harness or CI integration). Candidate said they had time constraints but agreed to clean up before offer.
- Pairing code quality: clear, well-named functions, thoughtful comments. Minimal edge-case tests during pairing — note to ask for a small unit test addition in follow-up.

Behavioral fit / signals:
- Highly collaborative, intentionally asks clarifying Qs, and biases toward shipping with safety nets.
- Mentions mentoring junior engineers frequently — good match for a mid-size org where we need seniors to scale the team.
- Cultural signal: pragmatic, low-ego, enjoys debugging with others.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: limited end-to-end benchmarking experience on heterogeneous GPU fleet.
  Mitigation: Pair early with performance engineer (assign buddy); require a 30/60/90 plan to own one perf regression and build a CI microbenchmark.
- Risk: take-home lacked CI.
  Mitigation: require candidate to submit a short follow-up gdoc with commands to reproduce and a simple flamegraph; treat as a post-loop condition of hire.

Open questions for references / hiring committee:
- Did they own capacity planning conversations (e.g., predicting throughput needs months out)?
- How do they instrument micro-latency changes — examples of dashboards / alerting rules they authored?
- Was there a postmortem where they introduced a fix that caused a regression? How did they handle rollback and communication?

Suggested next steps (practical):
1) Reference check (esp. on perf/regression ownership) — ask direct question about benchmarking ownership. (Owner: Miguel)
2) Quick ask to candidate: add 1-2 lines to the take-home doc showing commands to run the perf sample and one flamegraph PNG. Deadline: 48h.
3) If references are good, extend offer with standard band (SWE III / Senior) and a 6-month perf onboarding goal: own a microbenchmark + reduce tail P99 for one route by 10%.

Logistics / comp notes:
- Candidate expects mid-band comp for SF; flexible on equity. We should confirm by recruiter.
- Start date target: mid-Jan (stated preference).

Micro-attachments / links I left in the pairing doc:
- snippet: batching pseudocode he preferred (I pasted into GH-PR-4823)
- perf note: candidate's notes on adaptive batching algorithm (copied to CONFLUENCE-ENG/serve-runtime-oncall-runbook under 'candidate-notes')

Final gut: hire. Lean: strong technical + product sense; manageable perf skill gaps easily covered by pair-programming and explicit 90-day deliverable.

Action items (for me):
- Send ref questionnaire to listed manager within 24h.
- Reply to candidate with the 48h small artifact ask.
- Add to hiring thread with a one-paragraph synthesis and recommended band.

---
Scratch thoughts / ephemeral: 
- If we don't hire, risk is losing a calm senior who can stabilize oncall chatter. Could be hard to replace for hire curve.
- If we do hire, plan a week with infra + SRE pairing, and a perf project owner.

End of notes.
